findings.claim: "Professor James Reason's work on human error and patient safety — specifically his distinction between person-centred and system-centred approaches to error — is cited as the intellectual foundation of the guide" (Source: ... Preamble and title block)
findings.failure_mode: asserts the source cites a specific Reason concept; the deep ref states it cites none. Also mis-locates the attribution
findings.evidence: Deep 165: 'Reason is named once, in the source's footer; no specific work or concept of Reason's is cited by name' [BT]. Deep 182: further characterisation of the lineage 'is outside the scope ... because it is not stated in the source'. Source line 122: the attribution is in the footer ('Attribution and provenance'), not the preamble.
findings.fix: correct: "First, the poster's footer names 'the work of Professor James Reason' as a basis for the guide; no specific work or concept of Reason's is cited, and his publications are not held in this corpus." and change the citation to (Source: Footer)

findings.claim: Q1 is "the rare path where police, regulatory bodies (DPA, GDPR enforcement, sectoral regulators), and disciplinary processes are on the table."
findings.failure_mode: implies exclusivity for actions that also appear on the G branch
findings.evidence: Deep 144 [V] (Q5, 'Recommendation G'): 'may require relevant regulatory bodies to be contacted, staff suspension and disciplinary processes'. Only police referral is unique to Recommendation A (deep 96).
findings.fix: correct: "the rare path where police referral is on the table, alongside regulatory bodies (DPA, GDPR enforcement, sectoral regulators) and disciplinary processes, which the residual G branch can also reach"

findings.claim: "In software-business terms, the residual after all system filters is rare; most software incidents route to Recommendation D or E." Same register: line 14 'the most common software-incident failure mode'; line 26 'In software the most common positive findings are mental-health load, on-call exhaustion, and burnout'; line 28 'are the routine pattern'; line 66 'The vast majority of software incidents clear this filter at No'; line 207 'the dominant outcomes for software incidents'.
findings.failure_mode: frequency and outcome claims about software incidents presented as fact, with no source in the corpus
findings.evidence: Deep 152: 'The source carries no quantitative claims — no incidence rates, no outcome statistics'. No other deep ref consulted carries software-incident distributions; the distillation's own line 199 says the software mapping is 'a distillation-level analogy-transfer'.
findings.fix: correct: recast each as the operator's expectation, e.g. line 32 "In software-business terms the operator should expect the residual to be rare and most cases to exit at D or E (a distillation-level expectation, not a source finding)."; strip 'most common', 'routine pattern', 'vast majority' and 'dominant' where no expectation framing is added

findings.claim: "The substitution test anchors blameless post-mortem practice" / Q4 "maps to the would-another-engineer-have-done-the-same test that anchors blameless post-mortem practice"
findings.failure_mode: claims a relationship between the substitution test and blameless post-mortem practice that no corpus deep ref carries
findings.evidence: NHS deep 72-80 describes the substitution test without reference to post-mortems. OPL deep 237 and 314 describe Blameless Postmortem ('Our job is not to point fingers at an unlucky engineer ...') with no substitution test.
findings.fix: correct: "The substitution test's question sits close to the blameless-postmortem stance the Open Practice Library describes ('Our job is not to point fingers at an unlucky engineer', OPL, Practice 'Blameless Postmortem') — a distillation-level parallel."

findings.claim: "The just-culture default-to-system prior, combined with the wider-investigation parallel, is the structural mechanism by which an engineering organisation builds (or destroys) the psychological safety that surfaces near-misses, dissent, and bad-news signals."
findings.failure_mode: causal mechanism attributed to the source's framework that the source does not state
findings.evidence: The NHS deep ref contains no reference to psychological safety, near-misses, dissent or bad-news signals. Its closest claim is the dual purpose, 'protecting staff from unfair targeting' [V] (deep 19, 38). The task spec (tasks/software-business.md line 56) names this source for 'psychological-safety + authority-gradient' as routing, which is not a source claim.
findings.fix: correct: "The just-culture default-to-system prior, with its stated aim of 'protecting staff from unfair targeting' [V], bears on how an engineering organisation responds when something goes wrong; its link to psychological safety is a distillation-level reading, not a claim the source makes."

findings.claim: Route the rest through openstax-organizational-behavior and openstax-principles-management distillations, "which carry the broader psychological-safety and Theory-X-vs-Theory-Y treatments"; line 144 routes 'general psychological-safety design' to the same two sources.
findings.failure_mode: attributes a psychological-safety treatment to sources whose deep refs do not carry one
findings.evidence: Theory X/Y is supported (OB deep 392, 689; PoM deep 622, 948). 'psychological safety' has no hit in either deep ref; among demo deep refs it appears only in open-practice-library-deep.md (line 110).
findings.fix: correct: "... which carry the broader Theory-X-vs-Theory-Y treatment; for psychological-safety practices, see open-practice-library" (apply the same change at line 144)

findings.section: What to Look For, row 6 (and Anti-patterns line 175)
findings.claim: HR escalation opening before the tree is walked means "HR is replacing the just-culture decision"; follow-up: "Pause the HR escalation until the tree has been walked".
findings.failure_mode: inverts a one-way caveat and ranks the guide ahead of HR, against the source's 'in conjunction with'
findings.evidence: Source line 13 / deep 29 [V]: the guide 'does not replace HR advice and should be used in conjunction with organisational policy.' The caveat is that the guide does not replace HR; it gives no precedence over HR. Line 175 itself says HR runs 'alongside, not instead of' the decision, which conflicts with 'pause'.
findings.fix: correct: follow-up "Run the tree alongside the HR process, not after it; the guide does not replace HR advice and should be used in conjunction with organisational policy (Preamble, 'Please note', bullet 3)"; apply the same at line 175

findings.section: Anti-patterns: Skipping Q2 on impaired engineers (and lines 12, 126)
findings.claim: "the source's frame treats workload-induced impairment as a Q2 condition for the response"; line 12: Q2's response is "occupational-health and substance-abuse-at-work pathways, not sanction"; line 126: "the response is occupational-health, not procedural tightening".
findings.failure_mode: attributes the distillation's analogy (burnout/exhaustion as ill health) to the source, and adds exclusions the recommendations do not make
findings.evidence: Deep 56-58 [V]: Q2 asks about 'indications of substance abuse', 'physical ill health', 'mental ill health'; workload or fatigue is not named. Deep 104 [V] B: 'Follow organisational substance abuse at work guidance' (no statement that this excludes sanction). Deep 112 [V] C pairs organisational health guidance with a wider investigation, which can include procedural change.
findings.fix: correct (line 171): "Follow-up: route back to Q2 if the workload has produced indications of physical or mental ill health (the distillation's reading of Q2); pair it with the source's system question: could the health issue have been recognised and addressed earlier?"; strip 'not sanction' (line 12) and 'not procedural tightening' (line 126)

findings.claim: The CTO marks 3b as No because "the protocol was honoured in letter but not in the safety property it was meant to provide."
findings.failure_mode: worked example misapplies sub-question 3b; the scenario's facts fit 3c
findings.evidence: Deep 67 [V] 3b: 'Were the protocols/accepted practice workable and in routine use?' In the scenario the review policy was workable and in routine use and the engineer complied with it, so 3b is Yes; deep 68 [V] 3c ('Did the individual knowingly depart from these protocols?') is the No. The routing to Recommendation D is still correct.
findings.fix: correct: "3b (workable and in routine use — yes, as written). 3c (did the engineer knowingly depart? — no: the change had the senior review the policy required; the policy simply did not require reviewer independence). 3c is No; the tree routes to Recommendation D."

findings.claim: "The Army AAR carries the blameless review facilitation discipline. Use TC 25-20 to facilitate the blameless post-mortem"
findings.failure_mode: imported label; TC 25-20's deep ref does not frame the AAR as blameless
findings.evidence: No 'blame' or 'blameless' hit in tc-25-20-army-aar-deep.md. Its frame is 'not a critique' and 'does not grade success or failure' [V] (deep 253), and discovery by participants (deep 25, 35).
findings.fix: correct: "The Army AAR carries the not-a-critique, discovery-by-participants facilitation discipline ('does not grade success or failure' [V]). Use TC 25-20 to facilitate the post-incident review ..."

findings.section: Integration with Other References (OpenStax Business Ethics)
findings.claim: "the just-culture wider-investigation parallel is an ethical-maximum response — the individual response is the minimum, the system response is the maximum"
findings.failure_mode: forced mapping of Business Ethics' terms onto the individual/system split
findings.evidence: Business Ethics deep 107 [V]: ethical maximum is 'the strongest action a company can choose to behave ethically in a given situation'; ethical minimum is 'the least a company might do'. Neither deep ref equates an individual-directed response with the ethical minimum.
findings.fix: correct: "OpenStax distinguishes the moral minimum, ethical minimum and ethical maximum (Ch 3.1, Ch 4); pairing any individual response with a wider system investigation reads as going beyond the minimum (a distillation-level reading)."

findings.claim: "the deep reference classifies its claims as [V] (verbatim from the poster's text) or [AR] (the distillation team's paraphrase of the poster's reasoning)"
findings.failure_mode: marker definition wrong and marker set incomplete
findings.evidence: docs/architecture/ingestion-protocol.md line 31: [AR] = author argument. The deep ref also uses [AP] (4 occurrences, e.g. deep 17, 28) and [BT] (deep 165-166).
findings.fix: correct: "the deep reference classifies its claims as [V] (verbatim), [AP] (author paraphrase), [AR] (author argument: the poster's reasoning as reconstructed at ingestion) and [BT] (the footer lineage)"

findings.failure_mode: names lens-spec vocabulary the lens spec does not contain
